name: How much does a garage conversion actually cost in Los Angeles in 2026?

mainEntity.name: How much does a garage conversion cost in Los Angeles if the garage already has a slab, electricity, and a newer roof?
mainEntity.text: How much does a garage conversion cost in Los Angeles if the garage already has a slab, electricity, and a newer roof?

acceptedAnswer.text: The biggest cost driver in a garage conversion is not the square footage alone, but how much of the existing structure can be reused. A garage with a sound slab, solid framing, and an upgraded roof can save significant money because the project avoids major shell construction. Even then, a legal conversion usually still needs insulation, drywall, new electrical, plumbing if adding a bath or kitchen, HVAC, fire-rated assemblies, egress-compliant openings, and permit drawings. In Los Angeles, buyers often underestimate soft costs such as surveys, engineering, title review, plan check, and utility upgrades. The best way to budget is to separate the project into three buckets: reuse of the existing shell, required code upgrades, and finish level. A cosmetic conversion and a fully permitted ADU are not the same cost. If the garage has water intrusion, low ceiling height, cracked slab, or outdated wiring, those conditions can push the price up quickly. A realistic estimate should come from a site walk and plan set, not a square-foot shortcut alone.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage conversion in Los Angeles usually costs less than building a new detached ADU, but the final price depends on structural repairs, insulation, plumbing, windows, HVAC, and finish level. Projects with an intact shell can stay closer to the lower end, while older garages with foundation, moisture, or code issues can rise sharply.
